propositions: Self-consistency test measures whether the Pass-2/Pass-3 judge's decision output is stable across repeated evaluations of the same finding, using a 3-vote consensus over 50 findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort, with a pass floor of κ≥0.6 AND raw agreement≥0.8.

Order-shuffle test measures whether the gate's verdict (PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE) is stable when the input plan's top-level sections are permuted in different orders, using 3 distinct permutations per plan over 14 permutable plans from the committed corpus, with an identical κ≥0.6 AND raw agreement≥0.8 floor.

Infra-INDETERMINATE votes/verdicts carrying coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed flags are treated as execution failures, not stable judge outcomes, and are re-run until a substantive decision is reached or the finding is excluded.

The experiment runs over frozen, committed input samples (e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl and e6_ordershuffle_inputs.jsonl) to enable reproducibility without live plan-text corpus or ticket-store dependencies at judge time.
Self-consistency test result gates R5's addition of the new asserted_capability_confirmed sub-answer; order-shuffle test result gates R3's container criterion addition as an R3 prerequisite.

The driver harness measures the existing gate's stochastic stability without modifying src/rebar code; Exp A reuses three_pass internal functions within a gate_source session with explicit repo_root, while Exp B drives the public review_plan entrypoint against a throwaway REBAR_TRACKER_DIR clone to vary section order without mutating the real ticket store.
